objects.definition:
struct InflateState {
	cc_uint8 State;
	cc_bool LastBlock; /* Whether the last DEFLATE block has been encounted in the stream */
	cc_uint32 Bits;    /* Holds bits across byte boundaries */
	cc_uint32 NumBits; /* Number of bits in Bits buffer */

	cc_uint8* NextIn;   /* Pointer within Input buffer to next byte that can be read */
	cc_uint32 AvailIn;  /* Max number of bytes that can be read from Input buffer */
	cc_uint8* Output;   /* Pointer for output data */
	cc_uint32 AvailOut; /* Max number of bytes that can be written to Output buffer */
	struct Stream* Source;  /* Source for filling Input buffer */

	cc_uint32 Index;                          /* General purpose index / counter */
	cc_uint32 WindowIndex;                    /* Current index within window circular buffer */
	cc_uint32 NumCodeLens, NumLits, NumDists; /* Temp counters */
	cc_uint32 TmpCodeLens, TmpLit, TmpDist;   /* Temp huffman codes */

	cc_uint8 Input[INFLATE_MAX_INPUT];       /* Buffer for input to DEFLATE */
	cc_uint8 Buffer[INFLATE_MAX_LITS_DISTS]; /* General purpose temp array */
	union {
		struct HuffmanTable CodeLens;       /* Values represent codeword lengths of lits/dists codewords */
		struct HuffmanTable Lits;           /* Values represent literal or lengths */
	} Table; /* union to save on memory */
	struct HuffmanTable TableDists;         /* Values represent distances back */
	cc_uint8 Window[INFLATE_WINDOW_SIZE];    /* Holds circular buffer of recent output data, used for LZ77 */
	cc_result result;
};
objects.description: Streaming DEFLATE decompressor state, including bit-buffer, I/O cursors, temporary buffers, Huffman tables, and LZ77 sliding window. Use with Inflate_Init2, Inflate_Process, and Inflate_MakeStream2.
Streaming DEFLATE compressor state, including bit-buffer, output staging, codebook storage, and LZ77 hash chains. Construct a write-only stream with Deflate_MakeStream.

functions.name: Math_AbsF
functions.signature: float Math_AbsF(float x);
functions.description: Returns the absolute value of a single-precision float. Note: This may be defined as a macro mapping to a compiler intrinsic on some platforms, or as a function otherwise. Use to strip the sign from x.
requirements: x may be any finite float value; NaN handling is implementation-defined due to potential macro/intrinsic expansion.

functions.name: Math_SqrtF
functions.signature: float Math_SqrtF(float x);
functions.description: Returns the square root of a single-precision float. Note: This may be defined as a macro mapping to a compiler intrinsic on some platforms, or as a function otherwise.
requirements: x should be >= 0 for a real result; negative inputs yield implementation-defined results (NaN on most platforms).
Behavior and errno/exception semantics may differ when implemented as a macro/intrinsic.

functions.name: Math_Mod1
functions.signature: float Math_Mod1(float x);
functions.description: Computes x modulo 1.0 (the fractional part wrapped into [0,1)). Typical use: normalize a value to a unit interval (e.g., texture coordinate wrapping). Exact behavior for negative x is not documented but generally returns a value in [0,1).
requirements: x may be any float; if negative inputs are used, caller should not assume a specific rounding mode beyond typical mod-1 wrapping semantics (details are unknown).

functions.name: Math_SafeDiv
functions.signature: static inline float Math_SafeDiv(float a, float b);
functions.description: Performs a safe float division a / b. If |b| < 1e-6, returns a large sentinel value (1e9) instead of dividing to avoid overflow/NaN. Useful when denominators may approach zero.
requirements: No special requirements; function is total over all finite inputs.
Callers should check for the sentinel value (1e9) to detect near-zero denominator cases if that matters to logic.

functions.name: Math_Sin
functions.signature: CC_API double Math_Sin(double x);
functions.description: Computes the sine of x (radians). Double-precision variant of sine.
requirements: x is in radians; any finite double is accepted.

functions.name: Math_Cos
functions.signature: CC_API double Math_Cos(double x);
functions.description: Computes the cosine of x (radians). Double-precision variant of cosine.
requirements: x is in radians; any finite double is accepted.

functions.name: Math_SinF
functions.signature: CC_API float Math_SinF(float x);
functions.description: Computes the sine of x (radians). Single-precision variant.
requirements: x is in radians; any finite float is accepted.

functions.name: Math_CosF
functions.signature: CC_API float Math_CosF(float x);
functions.description: Computes the cosine of x (radians). Single-precision variant.
requirements: x is in radians; any finite float is accepted.

functions.name: Math_Atan2f
functions.signature: float Math_Atan2f(float x, float y);
functions.description: Computes atan2(y, x), primarily for angle calculation. Note: accuracy is only up to around 4 decimal places. Although parameters are named (x, y), the function computes atan2 with the conventional order (y, x).
requirements: x and y may be any finite floats.
Callers should not rely on precision beyond ~4 decimal places.

functions.name: Math_Log2
functions.signature: double Math_Log2(double x);
functions.description: Computes log base 2 of x. Can be used to approximate log_y(x) via log2(x)/log2(y).
requirements: x must be > 0 for a real result; non-positive inputs lead to implementation-defined results (typically -inf or NaN).

functions.name: Math_Exp2
functions.signature: double Math_Exp2(double x);
functions.description: Computes 2 raised to the power x. Can be used with Math_Log2 to compute y^x via exp2(log2(y)*x).
requirements: x may be any finite double; large |x| may overflow/underflow to infinities/zero.

functions.name: Math_Floor
functions.signature: int Math_Floor(float value);
functions.description: Returns the greatest integer less than or equal to value, as a 32-bit int.
requirements: value may be any float; if outside int range, behavior of conversion/truncation is implementation-defined.

functions.name: Math_Ceil
functions.signature: int Math_Ceil(float value);
functions.description: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to value, as a 32-bit int.
requirements: value may be any float; if outside int range, behavior of conversion/truncation is implementation-defined.

functions.name: Math_ilog2
functions.signature: int Math_ilog2(cc_uint32 value);
functions.description: Returns the integer base-2 logarithm of value (index of the highest set bit). Commonly used to determine bit widths or mip levels.
requirements: value must be > 0; ilog2(0) is undefined/invalid.

functions.name: Math_CeilDiv
functions.signature: int Math_CeilDiv(int a, int b);
functions.description: Returns the ceiling of integer division a / b. Useful for chunking and sizing when partial division should round up.
requirements: b must not be 0.

Behavior with negative operands follows the implementation’s chosen rounding semantics for ceiling division; callers should avoid negative divisors/operands if they require specific semantics (details are unknown).

functions.name: Math_Sign
functions.signature: int Math_Sign(float value);
functions.description: Returns the sign of value as an int. Typically -1 for negative, 0 for zero, and 1 for positive.
requirements: value may be any float; exact mapping for NaN is unknown.

functions.name: Math_ClampAngle
functions.signature: float Math_ClampAngle(float degrees);
functions.description: Clamps an angle in degrees into the range [0, 360). Useful for normalizing angles for rendering or physics.
requirements: Input is an angle in degrees. Any finite float accepted.

functions.name: Math_Lerp
functions.signature: float Math_Lerp(float a, float b, float t);
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between a and b using parameter t. Result is a + t*(b - a).
requirements: t in [0,1] yields interpolation; values outside will extrapolate.
All inputs may be any finite floats.

functions.name: Math_LerpAngle
functions.signature: float Math_LerpAngle(float leftAngle, float rightAngle, float t);
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between two angles (degrees), adjusting wrap-around as necessary to take the shortest path. Useful for smooth rotations.
requirements: Angles are in degrees.
t in [0,1] yields interpolation; values outside will extrapolate.

functions.name: Math_NextPowOf2
functions.signature: int Math_NextPowOf2(int value);
functions.description: Returns the next power-of-two greater than or equal to value. If value is already a power of two, it is typically returned unchanged.
requirements: value should be > 0; behavior for non-positive values is unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: Math_IsPowOf2
functions.signature: cc_bool Math_IsPowOf2(int value);
functions.description: Returns whether value is a power of two.
requirements: value should be > 0 to be considered a power of two; non-positive inputs return false or are invalid (exact behavior for <= 0 is unknown).

functions.name: Random_SeedFromCurrentTime
functions.signature: void Random_SeedFromCurrentTime(RNGState* rnd);
functions.description: Initializes the RNG state using a seed derived from the current UTC time. Use before generating random numbers if you want time-based seeding.
requirements: rnd must be a non-NULL pointer to RNGState storage.
Must be called before Random_Next/Random_Float/Random_Range if no other seeding is performed.

functions.name: Random_Seed
functions.signature: CC_API void Random_Seed(RNGState* rnd, int seed);
functions.description: Initializes the RNG state using the provided seed. Deterministic across runs for the same seed and implementation.
requirements: rnd must be a non-NULL pointer to RNGState storage.
Should be called before Random_Next/Random_Float/Random_Range to initialize the state.

functions.name: Random_Next
functions.signature: CC_API int Random_Next(RNGState* rnd, int n);
functions.description: Returns a pseudo-random integer in the range [0, n). Advances the RNG state.
requirements: rnd must be a valid, initialized RNG state (seeded via Random_Seed or Random_SeedFromCurrentTime).
n must be > 0; n <= 0 is invalid and may cause undefined behavior.

functions.name: Random_Float
functions.signature: CC_API float Random_Float(RNGState* rnd);
functions.description: Returns a pseudo-random float in the range [0.0, 1.0). Advances the RNG state.
requirements: rnd must be a valid, initialized RNG state (seeded via Random_Seed or Random_SeedFromCurrentTime).

functions.name: Random_Range
functions.signature: static inline int Random_Range(RNGState* rnd, int min, int max);
functions.description: Returns a pseudo-random integer in the range [min, max). Implemented as min + Random_Next(rnd, max - min). Advances the RNG state.
requirements: rnd must be a valid, initialized RNG state (seeded).
max must be greater than min; if max <= min the call is invalid and may cause undefined behavior due to passing a non-positive bound to Random_Next.

functions.description: Encodes binary data to Base64. Converts blocks of 3 bytes into 4 ASCII characters, padding as required. Returns the number of ASCII characters written.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes (len can be 0).
dst must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the Base64 output. You MUST ensure that dst is appropriately sized.
Output length will be 4 * ceil(len / 3). Caller must size dst accordingly.

functions.name: Convert_FromBase64
functions.signature: int Convert_FromBase64(const char* src, int len, cc_uint8* dst);
functions.description: Decodes Base64 ASCII data into binary. Converts blocks of 4 ASCII characters into up to 3 bytes. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: src must point to a buffer of at least len characters containing Base64 text (padding handling and whitespace rules unknown).
dst must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the decoded bytes. You MUST ensure that dst is appropriately sized.
Maximum output length is 3 * (len / 4). Caller must size dst accordingly.

functions.name: EntryList_Load
functions.signature: CC_NOINLINE cc_result EntryList_Load(struct StringsBuffer* list, const char* file, char separator, EntryList_Filter filter);
functions.description: Loads key/value entries from a file on disk into a StringsBuffer. If separator is '\0', duplicate key checking is disabled. An optional filter callback can skip loading some entries.
requirements: list must point to an initialized StringsBuffer to be populated.
file must be a valid, null-terminated path to the file to read.
separator determines how keys/values are split; if '\0', duplicates are not checked.
filter may be NULL to load all entries; when non-NULL, it will be called to decide whether to include entries.
Returns a cc_result status code; callers should check for success/failure per project conventions.

functions.name: EntryList_UNSAFE_Load
functions.signature: CC_NOINLINE cc_result EntryList_UNSAFE_Load(struct StringsBuffer* list, const char* file);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for EntryList_Load using a separator of '\0' and filter of NULL. Does not check for duplicate keys.
requirements: list must point to an initialized StringsBuffer to be populated.
file must be a valid, null-terminated path to the file to read.
Duplicate key checking is not performed; callers must tolerate or resolve duplicates themselves.
Returns a cc_result status code; callers should check for success/failure per project conventions.

functions.name: EntryList_Save
functions.signature: CC_NOINLINE void EntryList_Save(struct StringsBuffer* list, const char* file);
functions.description: Saves the entries contained in the given StringsBuffer to disk at the specified path.
requirements: list must point to a valid, initialized StringsBuffer containing entries to write.
file must be a valid, null-terminated path; parent directories must exist unless created elsewhere (unknown).
Callers should handle any I/O errors according to project logging/error mechanisms (unknown specifics).

functions.name: EntryList_Remove
functions.signature: CC_NOINLINE cc_bool EntryList_Remove(struct StringsBuffer* list, const cc_string* key, char separator);
functions.description: Removes the entry whose key caselessly equals the given key. Returns true if an entry was removed, false otherwise.
requirements: list must point to a valid StringsBuffer.
key must be a valid cc_string representing the key to remove.
separator indicates the separator used by entries; should match how entries were loaded/saved.

functions.name: EntryList_Set
functions.signature: CC_NOINLINE void EntryList_Set(struct StringsBuffer* list, const cc_string* key, const cc_string* value, char separator);
functions.description: Replaces the entry whose key caselessly equals the given key with a new value, or adds a new entry if no existing key matches.
requirements: list must point to a valid StringsBuffer to modify.
key must be a valid cc_string; comparison is case-insensitive.
value must be a valid cc_string to store for the key.
separator indicates how key/value are separated in serialized form; should be consistent with load/save.

functions.name: EntryList_UNSAFE_Get
functions.signature: CC_NOINLINE STRING_REF cc_string EntryList_UNSAFE_Get(struct StringsBuffer* list, const cc_string* key, char separator);
functions.description: Returns the value of the entry whose key caselessly equals the given key. Marked UNSAFE, likely returning a reference tied to internal storage of the StringsBuffer.
requirements: list must point to a valid StringsBuffer containing entries.
key must be a valid cc_string for lookup; comparison is case-insensitive.
Returned cc_string likely aliases internal storage; its lifetime is tied to list and may become invalid after list mutation (inferred).
separator should match the format of entries in the list.

functions.name: EntryList_Find
functions.signature: CC_NOINLINE int EntryList_Find(struct StringsBuffer* list, const cc_string* key, char separator);
functions.description: Finds the index of the entry whose key caselessly equals the given key. Returns the zero-based index on success, or a negative/implementation-defined value if not found (exact sentinel unknown).
requirements: list must point to a valid StringsBuffer.
key must be a valid cc_string for lookup; comparison is case-insensitive.
separator should match the format used in the list.

functions.name: BitmapColor_Offset
functions.signature: BitmapCol BitmapColor_Offset(BitmapCol color, int rBy, int gBy, int bBy);
functions.description: Adjusts a packed color by adding per-channel offsets to the R, G, and B components. Intended for simple brightness/tint operations on a single BitmapCol value. Details such as clamping/overflow behavior are not documented in this header and are unknown.
requirements: color must be a valid BitmapCol value as used by this library.
rBy, gBy, bBy are integer offsets applied to the R, G, and B channels; exact clamping or wrap behavior is unknown.

functions.name: BitmapColor_Scale
functions.signature: BitmapCol BitmapColor_Scale(BitmapCol a, float t);
functions.description: Scales the RGB (and possibly alpha) components of a packed color by a scalar factor t. Useful for dimming or amplifying a color. Whether scaling applies to alpha and how results are clamped is not documented and is unknown.
requirements: a must be a valid BitmapCol value as used by this library.
t is a floating-point scale factor; acceptable range and clamping behavior are unknown.

functions.name: Bitmap_UNSAFE_CopyBlock
functions.signature: void Bitmap_UNSAFE_CopyBlock(int srcX, int srcY, int dstX, int dstY, struct Bitmap* src, struct Bitmap* dst, int size);
functions.description: Copies a block of pixels from a source bitmap to a destination bitmap. Labeled UNSAFE because bounds are not checked and overlapping copies in the same bitmap are forbidden. The parameter size appears to indicate the (square) block dimension in pixels; exact shape semantics are not documented and are inferred from the name.
requirements: If src and dst are the same bitmap, the source and destination rectangles must not overlap.
Caller must ensure the source and destination rectangles lie fully within their respective bitmaps; no bounds checking is performed.
src and dst must point to initialised Bitmap instances with valid scan0 buffers.
size must correspond to the intended block extent; exact interpretation is not documented. Use only values that keep rectangles within bounds.
Coordinates (srcX, srcY) and (dstX, dstY) are in pixels and must be non-negative indices within the respective bitmaps for the chosen block extent.

functions.name: Bitmap_Allocate
functions.signature: void Bitmap_Allocate(struct Bitmap* bmp, int width, int height);
functions.description: Allocates pixel storage for a bitmap of the given dimensions and assigns it to bmp. The caller is responsible for freeing the allocated memory. Behavior on invalid dimensions or allocation failure is not documented here.
requirements: bmp must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a Bitmap struct.
width and height should specify the desired bitmap dimensions; acceptable ranges and overflow handling are not documented.
Caller is responsible for freeing the allocated memory for the bitmap; the exact deallocation API is not specified in this header.
bmp should not reference an existing allocation unless the caller will free/overwrite it appropriately before calling.

functions.name: Bitmap_TryAllocate
functions.signature: void Bitmap_TryAllocate(struct Bitmap* bmp, int width, int height);
functions.description: Attempts to allocate pixel storage for a bitmap of the given dimensions and assigns it to bmp. Like Bitmap_Allocate, but intended to handle allocation failures more gracefully. Exact failure signaling (e.g., setting scan0 to NULL) is not documented and is unknown.
requirements: bmp must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a Bitmap struct.
width and height should specify the desired bitmap dimensions; acceptable ranges and overflow handling are not documented.
Caller is responsible for freeing any allocated memory; the exact deallocation API is not specified in this header.
Caller must check bmp after the call to determine success/failure; exact indicators of failure are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: Bitmap_Scale
functions.signature: CC_API void Bitmap_Scale(struct Bitmap* dst, struct Bitmap* src, int srcX, int srcY, int srcWidth, int srcHeight);
functions.description: Scales a rectangular region of the source bitmap (srcX, srcY, srcWidth, srcHeight) to fill the entire destination bitmap dst. Can scale up or down depending on dst dimensions. Useful for image resizing and thumbnail generation.
requirements: dst must be an initialised Bitmap with a valid scan0 buffer and intended output width/height set.
src must be an initialised Bitmap with a valid scan0 buffer.
The rectangle defined by (srcX, srcY, srcWidth, srcHeight) must lie entirely within src; no bounds checking is documented.
dst’s dimensions determine the output size; caller must ensure dst has been allocated to the desired size before calling.

functions.name: Png_Detect
functions.signature: cc_bool Png_Detect(const cc_uint8* data, cc_uint32 len);
functions.description: Returns whether the provided data buffer begins with the PNG file signature. Intended for quick format sniffing before decoding.
requirements: data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes; must not be NULL when len > 0.
For a definitive check, len should be at least PNG_SIG_SIZE (8) bytes; with fewer bytes, detection may fail or be inconclusive.
Function examines only the prefix; it does not validate full PNG structure.

functions.name: Png_Decode
functions.signature: CC_API cc_result Png_Decode(struct Bitmap* bmp, struct Stream* stream);
functions.description: Decodes a PNG image from the provided stream into a bitmap. On success, bmp is populated with the decoded image. Based in part on references cited in the comments. Exact memory ownership details are not stated here, but typically the resulting pixel buffer becomes caller-owned for later freeing.
requirements: bmp must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a Bitmap to receive the decoded image.
stream must be a valid input stream positioned at the start of PNG data (or at least before the PNG signature).
Returned cc_result must be checked by the caller for success/failure; exact error codes are defined elsewhere.
Image dimension limits may apply (e.g., PNG_MAX_DIMS); inputs exceeding limits may fail to decode (limit is declared in this header).
On success, caller is responsible for managing/freeing any allocated pixel memory in bmp; exact deallocation API is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: Png_Encode
functions.signature: cc_result Png_Encode(struct Bitmap* bmp, struct Stream* stream, Png_RowGetter getRow, cc_bool alpha, void* ctx);
functions.description: Encodes a bitmap to PNG format and writes it to stream. A custom row getter callback may be supplied to modify per-row data access (e.g., for flipping). If alpha is non-zero, RGBA is saved; otherwise only RGB channels are written.
requirements: bmp must be an initialised Bitmap with valid pixel data.
stream must be a valid, writable stream capable of receiving PNG data.
getRow may be NULL; when non-NULL it must return a pointer to the requested row compatible with the bitmap format and may use ctx.
alpha controls whether the alpha channel is included (non-zero) or RGB-only is written (zero).
Caller must check the returned cc_result for success/failure; exact error codes are defined elsewhere.

functions.name: GZipHeader_Init
functions.signature: void GZipHeader_Init(struct GZipHeader* header);
functions.description: Initializes a GZipHeader structure to its default state before parsing a GZIP header. Use this before GZipHeader_Read when you need to skip or parse a GZIP header prior to DEFLATE decompression.
requirements: header must be a valid, writable pointer to a GZipHeader structure
Call this before the first call to GZipHeader_Read for the same header object

functions.name: GZipHeader_Read
functions.signature: cc_result GZipHeader_Read(struct Stream* s, struct GZipHeader* header);
functions.description: Parses/consumes a GZIP header from the input stream, updating the provided GZipHeader state. Use to skip a GZIP header so that subsequent DEFLATE-only processing can begin at the compressed data.
requirements: s must be a valid readable Stream positioned at the beginning of a GZIP-compressed payload (i.e., at the start of the GZIP header)
header must point to a valid GZipHeader structure, typically initialized with GZipHeader_Init
On success, the stream position advances past the GZIP header; callers should then feed the following DEFLATE data to a DEFLATE decoder
The function returns a cc_result status code; non-zero indicates an error and the caller should stop or handle the error accordingly

functions.name: Inflate_Init2
functions.signature: CC_API void Inflate_Init2(struct InflateState* state, struct Stream* source);
functions.description: Initializes an InflateState for DEFLATE decompression and associates it with a source stream for input. Call this before using the low-level Inflate_Process or before turning it into a read-only stream with Inflate_MakeStream2.
requirements: state must be a valid, writable pointer to an InflateState structure
source must be a valid readable Stream providing pure DEFLATE-compressed data (no GZIP/ZLIB headers)
Call this exactly once per InflateState instance before other Inflate operations on that instance

functions.name: Inflate_Process
functions.signature: void Inflate_Process(struct InflateState* s);
functions.description: Low-level routine that attempts to decompress as much pending DEFLATE data as possible using the provided InflateState. Typically you should not call this directly; prefer wrapping as a stream via Inflate_MakeStream2.
requirements: s must be a valid InflateState previously initialized via Inflate_Init2
This is a low-level API; callers are responsible for providing/maintaining appropriate input/output buffers in the state (details of buffer preparation and consumption are not documented here)
Intended for advanced use; typical usage should employ Inflate_MakeStream2 instead

functions.name: Inflate_MakeStream2
functions.signature: CC_API void Inflate_MakeStream2(struct Stream* stream, struct InflateState* state, struct Stream* underlying);
functions.description: Wraps an InflateState as a read-only Stream that reads pure DEFLATE-compressed data from an underlying stream and exposes decompressed bytes to callers. Use this when you need a streaming interface to DEFLATE decompression.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable Stream object to be initialized as a read-only decompression stream
state must be a valid InflateState (initialize with Inflate_Init2 or allow this function to set it up for streaming use)
underlying must be a valid readable Stream that yields pure DEFLATE data (no GZIP/ZLIB headers)
If the source data begins with a GZIP or ZLIB header, the caller must first skip it (e.g., with GZipHeader_Read or ZLibHeader_Read) before using this stream

functions.name: Deflate_MakeStream
functions.signature: CC_API void Deflate_MakeStream(struct Stream* stream, struct DeflateState* state, struct Stream* underlying);
functions.description: Creates a write-only Stream that compresses written data with DEFLATE and writes the compressed bytes to an underlying stream. Produces pure DEFLATE data (no header/footer).
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable Stream object to be initialized as a write-only compression stream
state must be a valid, writable DeflateState structure
underlying must be a valid writable Stream to receive compressed output
The produced stream is write-only; callers must not attempt to read from it

functions.name: GZip_MakeStream
functions.signature: CC_API void GZip_MakeStream(struct Stream* stream, struct GZipState* state, struct Stream* underlying);
functions.description: Creates a write-only Stream that compresses data with DEFLATE and encapsulates it in GZIP format (GZIP header + DEFLATE data + GZIP footer) before writing to the underlying stream.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable Stream object to be initialized as a write-only compression stream
state must be a valid, writable GZipState structure
underlying must be a valid writable Stream to receive the GZIP-formatted output
The produced stream is write-only; callers must not attempt to read from it

functions.name: ZLib_MakeStream
functions.signature: CC_API void ZLib_MakeStream(struct Stream* stream, struct ZLibState* state, struct Stream* underlying);
functions.description: Creates a write-only Stream that compresses data with DEFLATE and encapsulates it in ZLIB format (ZLIB header + DEFLATE data + ZLIB footer) before writing to the underlying stream.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable Stream object to be initialized as a write-only compression stream
state must be a valid, writable ZLibState structure
underlying must be a valid writable Stream to receive the ZLIB-formatted output
The produced stream is write-only; callers must not attempt to read from it

functions.name: Zip_Extract
functions.signature: cc_result Zip_Extract(struct Stream* source, Zip_SelectEntry selector, Zip_ProcessEntry processor, struct ZipEntry* entries, int maxEntries);
functions.description: Iterates over entries in a .zip archive read from the source stream, optionally selects entries with a predicate, and processes selected entries via a callback. Minimal metadata can be stored in the provided entries array. Processing stops if the processor returns a non-zero error code.
requirements: source must be a valid readable Stream positioned at the beginning of a .zip archive
selector must be a valid function pointer that returns true for entries to be processed; returning false skips an entry without unnecessary seeks

processor must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked with the entry path, a data stream for that entry, and the ZipEntry metadata; if it returns non-zero, extraction stops and that error is propagated
The data Stream passed to processor may not be seekable; processor implementations must handle non-seekable streams
entries must point to an array of ZipEntry with capacity for at least maxEntries items
maxEntries must be a non-negative integer indicating the capacity of the entries array
The function returns a cc_result status code; non-zero indicates an error

functions.name: Stream_Read
functions.signature: CC_API cc_result Stream_Read(struct Stream* s, cc_uint8* buffer, cc_uint32 count);
functions.description: Reads up to count bytes from the stream, attempting to fully satisfy the request. Intended for callers who want a full read rather than a partial one from the underlying Stream::Read. Returns a cc_result status code.
requirements: s must point to an initialised Stream instance.
buffer must point to writable memory of at least count bytes.
The underlying stream must support reading (Stream::Read or equivalent must be set).
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success or failure.

functions.name: Stream_Write
functions.signature: CC_API cc_result Stream_Write(struct Stream* s, const cc_uint8* buffer, cc_uint32 count);
functions.description: Writes up to count bytes to the stream, attempting to fully write the requested amount. Returns a cc_result status code.
requirements: s must point to an initialised Stream instance.
buffer must point to readable memory of at least count bytes.
The underlying stream must support writing (Stream::Write or equivalent must be set).
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success or failure.

functions.name: Stream_Init
functions.signature: void Stream_Init(struct Stream* s);
functions.description: Initialises default function pointers for a Stream so that operations are defined but will return an error for read/write/seek by default. Use before configuring a Stream with specific handlers.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a Stream to initialise.

functions.name: Stream_OpenFile
functions.signature: CC_API cc_result Stream_OpenFile(struct Stream* s, const cc_string* path);
functions.description: Opens a file located at path and wraps it as a Stream. This is a wrapper around Stream_OpenPath().
requirements: s must point to a Stream to receive the file-backed handlers.
path must point to a valid cc_string containing the file path.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success before using the stream.

functions.name: Stream_CreateFile
functions.signature: CC_API cc_result Stream_CreateFile(struct Stream* s, const cc_string* path);
functions.description: Creates (or overwrites) a file at path and wraps it as a Stream. This is a wrapper around Stream_CreatePath().
requirements: s must point to a Stream to receive the file-backed handlers.
path must point to a valid cc_string containing the file path.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success before using the stream.

functions.name: Stream_OpenPath
functions.signature: cc_result Stream_OpenPath(struct Stream* s, const cc_filepath* path);
functions.description: Opens a file at the given cc_filepath and wraps it into s using Stream_FromFile().
requirements: s must point to a Stream to initialise.
path must point to a valid cc_filepath.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success before using the stream.

functions.name: Stream_CreatePath
functions.signature: cc_result Stream_CreatePath(struct Stream* s, const cc_filepath* path);
functions.description: Creates (or overwrites) a file at the given cc_filepath and wraps it into s using Stream_FromFile().
requirements: s must point to a Stream to initialise.
path must point to a valid cc_filepath.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success before using the stream.

functions.name: Stream_AppendPath
functions.signature: cc_result Stream_AppendPath(struct Stream* s, const cc_filepath* path);
functions.description: Opens or creates a file, seeks to the end, and wraps it into s, enabling appending. Internally wraps File_OpenOrCreate and File_Seek(END) then Stream_FromFile().
requirements: s must point to a Stream to initialise.
path must point to a valid cc_filepath.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success before using the stream.

functions.name: Stream_WriteAllTo
functions.signature: cc_result Stream_WriteAllTo(const cc_string* path, const cc_uint8* data, cc_uint32 length);
functions.description: Creates or overwrites a file at path and writes exactly length bytes from data into it. Convenience one-shot write helper.
requirements: path must point to a valid cc_string containing the target file path.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success.

functions.name: Stream_FromFile
functions.signature: CC_API void Stream_FromFile(struct Stream* s, cc_file file);
functions.description: Configures s to wrap the given OS/file handle so it can be read/written/searched like a Stream.
requirements: s must point to a Stream to configure.
file must be a valid, open file handle compatible with the platform’s cc_file type.

functions.name: Stream_ReadonlyPortion
functions.signature: CC_API void Stream_ReadonlyPortion(struct Stream* s, struct Stream* source, cc_uint32 len);
functions.description: Wraps source and exposes a read-only stream that allows reading at most len bytes from the start of the wrapped source. Useful to restrict reads to a subrange.
requirements: s must point to a Stream to configure as the wrapper.
source must point to an initialised, readable Stream.
Only read operations are supported on the wrapper stream; writing is not supported.
len specifies the maximum readable byte count from the portion.

functions.name: Stream_ReadonlyMemory
functions.signature: CC_API void Stream_ReadonlyMemory(struct Stream* s, void* data, cc_uint32 len);
functions.description: Wraps a block of memory as a read-only, seekable stream of length len. Enables reading and seeking within the provided buffer.
requirements: s must point to a Stream to configure.
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
The resulting stream supports reading and seeking; writing is not supported.

functions.name: Stream_ReadonlyBuffered
functions.signature: CC_API void Stream_ReadonlyBuffered(struct Stream* s, struct Stream* source, void* data, cc_uint32 size);
functions.description: Wraps source with a buffered, read-only stream that reads through an intermediary buffer data of size bytes. Useful when underlying reads are expensive (e.g., files).
requirements: s must point to a Stream to configure.
source must point to an initialised, readable Stream.
data must point to a buffer of at least size bytes that remains valid for the stream’s lifetime or until reconfigured.
Only read operations are supported on the wrapper stream; writing is not supported.

functions.name: Stream_WriteonlyCrc32
functions.signature: void Stream_WriteonlyCrc32(struct Stream* s, struct Stream* source);
functions.description: Wraps source with a write-only stream that computes a running CRC32 over data written through it. To obtain the final CRC32, xor it with 0xFFFFFFFFUL.
requirements: s must point to a Stream to configure.
source must point to an initialised, writable Stream that will receive the written data.
Only write operations are supported on the wrapper stream; reading is not supported.
Callers are responsible for retrieving the computed CRC32 from the wrapper stream’s state; exact retrieval mechanism is not documented here.

functions.name: Stream_GetU16_LE
functions.signature: cc_uint16 Stream_GetU16_LE(const cc_uint8* data);
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit unsigned integer from memory in little-endian order.
requirements: data must point to at least 2 bytes of readable memory.

functions.name: Stream_GetU16_BE
functions.signature: cc_uint16 Stream_GetU16_BE(const cc_uint8* data);
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit unsigned integer from memory in big-endian order.
requirements: data must point to at least 2 bytes of readable memory.

functions.name: Stream_GetU32_LE
functions.signature: cc_uint32 Stream_GetU32_LE(const cc_uint8* data);
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit unsigned integer from memory in little-endian order.
requirements: data must point to at least 4 bytes of readable memory.

functions.name: Stream_GetU32_BE
functions.signature: cc_uint32 Stream_GetU32_BE(const cc_uint8* data);
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit unsigned integer from memory in big-endian order.
requirements: data must point to at least 4 bytes of readable memory.

functions.name: Stream_SetU16_LE
functions.signature: void Stream_SetU16_LE(cc_uint8* data, cc_uint16 value);
functions.description: Writes a 16-bit unsigned integer value to memory in little-endian order.
requirements: data must point to at least 2 bytes of writable memory.

functions.name: Stream_SetU16_BE
functions.signature: void Stream_SetU16_BE(cc_uint8* data, cc_uint16 value);
functions.description: Writes a 16-bit unsigned integer value to memory in big-endian order.
requirements: data must point to at least 2 bytes of writable memory.

functions.name: Stream_SetU32_LE
functions.signature: void Stream_SetU32_LE(cc_uint8* data, cc_uint32 value);
functions.description: Writes a 32-bit unsigned integer value to memory in little-endian order.
requirements: data must point to at least 4 bytes of writable memory.

functions.name: Stream_SetU32_BE
functions.signature: void Stream_SetU32_BE(cc_uint8* data, cc_uint32 value);
functions.description: Writes a 32-bit unsigned integer value to memory in big-endian order.
requirements: data must point to at least 4 bytes of writable memory.

functions.name: Stream_ReadU32_LE
functions.signature: cc_result Stream_ReadU32_LE(struct Stream* s, cc_uint32* value);
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit unsigned integer from the stream in little-endian order and stores it in value.
requirements: s must point to an initialised, readable Stream.
value must be a valid pointer to receive the 32-bit result.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success or failure.

functions.name: Stream_ReadU32_BE
functions.signature: cc_result Stream_ReadU32_BE(struct Stream* s, cc_uint32* value);
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit unsigned integer from the stream in big-endian order and stores it in value.
requirements: s must point to an initialised, readable Stream.
value must be a valid pointer to receive the 32-bit result.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success or failure.

functions.name: Stream_ReadLine
functions.signature: CC_API cc_result Stream_ReadLine(struct Stream* s, cc_string* text);
functions.description: Reads a line of UTF-8 encoded text from the stream into text. Reads one byte at a time; using Stream_ReadonlyBuffered may improve performance.
requirements: s must point to an initialised, readable Stream.
text must point to a cc_string to receive the line.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success or failure.

functions.name: Stream_WriteLine
functions.signature: CC_API cc_result Stream_WriteLine(struct Stream* s, cc_string* text);
functions.description: Writes a line of UTF-8 encoded text from text to the stream.
requirements: s must point to an initialised, writable Stream.
text must point to a cc_string containing the text to write.
Callers must check the returned cc_result for success or failure.

functions.name: MapImporter_Register
functions.signature: CC_API void MapImporter_Register(struct MapImporter* imp);
functions.description: Registers a map importer into the global list so that files with the importer's extension can be recognized and loaded. Typical usage: create and initialize a MapImporter instance (fileExt, import, next), then call this function during initialization to make the importer available.
requirements: imp must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
imp->fileExt should point to a valid, null-terminated file extension string for the format (e.g., ".cw").
imp->import must be a valid function pointer conforming to MapImportFunc and capable of importing the format.
imp->next is used for internal linked-list chaining and may be modified by the registration routine.
Thread-safety/duplicate registration behavior is unknown; callers should avoid concurrently registering from multiple threads unless explicitly synchronized (unknown in this header).

functions.name: MapImporter_Find
functions.signature: CC_API struct MapImporter* MapImporter_Find(const cc_string* path);
functions.description: Locates a registered map importer suitable for the given filename/path by matching its file extension. Returns NULL if no matching importer is found. Use this to look up which importer will handle a specific file before loading.
requirements: path must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a cc_string containing a filename or path.
The path string should include a file extension; otherwise, no importer may match and the function can return NULL.
Callers must check for a NULL return to handle the case where no importer supports the file.

functions.name: Map_LoadFrom
functions.signature: CC_API cc_result Map_LoadFrom(const cc_string* path);
functions.description: Attempts to import/load a map from the specified file path using a registered importer matched by the file's extension. This will read world data (and possibly metadata) encoded in that format into the running application.

The file's extension should correspond to a registered MapImporter; otherwise the load may fail.
Callers must handle the returned cc_result status code; non-zero (or implementation-defined) values indicate failure (exact error semantics unknown).
The current global/application state must be ready to receive a loaded world (exact prerequisites unknown).

functions.name: Cw_Save

requirements: stream must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a Stream open for writing.
The stream must remain valid for the duration of the call; ownership/lifetime is managed by the caller.
Seekability, endianness, and positioning requirements are unknown; if in doubt, position the stream at the desired start offset before calling.
Callers must check and handle the returned cc_result status code (exact error value conventions unknown).
A world must be available to export (precise prerequisites and selection of which world are unknown).

functions.name: Schematic_Save
functions.signature: cc_result Schematic_Save(struct Stream* stream);
functions.description: Exports the current world to a .schematic map file format (used by MCEdit and similar tools), writing the encoded data to the provided stream.
requirements: stream must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a Stream open for writing.
The stream must remain valid for the duration of the call; ownership/lifetime is managed by the caller.
Seekability and positioning requirements are unknown; if in doubt, position the stream at the intended start before calling.
Callers must check and handle the returned cc_result status code (exact error value conventions unknown).
A world must be available to export (precise prerequisites unknown).

functions.name: Dat_Save
functions.signature: cc_result Dat_Save(struct Stream* stream);
functions.description: Exports the current world to a .dat Classic map file format (used by Minecraft Classic), writing the encoded data to the provided stream.
requirements: stream must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a Stream open for writing.
The stream must remain valid for the duration of the call; ownership/lifetime is managed by the caller.
Seekability and positioning requirements are unknown; if in doubt, position the stream appropriately before calling.
Callers must check and handle the returned cc_result status code (exact error value conventions unknown).
A world must be available to export (precise prerequisites unknown).

functions.name: Logger_DialogWarn
functions.signature: void Logger_DialogWarn(const cc_string* msg);
functions.description: Displays a warning message box with the provided message. Intended for non-fatal user notifications, typically before the in-game chat system is available.
requirements: msg must point to a valid, initialized cc_string containing the text to display
msg must not be NULL

functions.name: Logger_FormatWarn
functions.signature: void Logger_FormatWarn(cc_string* msg, cc_result res, const char* action, Logger_DescribeError describeErr);
functions.description: Formats a warning message into msg using the pattern: "Error [result] when [action]\n  Error meaning: [desc]". If describeErr returns false, the 'Error meaning' line is omitted.
requirements: msg must be a valid, writable cc_string buffer capable of holding the formatted text
action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL) describing the operation that failed
describeErr, if non-NULL, must be a function matching Logger_DescribeError and safe to call with (res, dst)
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_FormatWarn2
functions.signature: void Logger_FormatWarn2(cc_string* msg, cc_result res, const char* action, const cc_string* path, Logger_DescribeError describeErr);
functions.description: Formats a warning message into msg using the pattern: "Error [result] when [action] '[path]'\n  Error meaning: [desc]". If describeErr returns false, the 'Error meaning' line is omitted.
requirements: msg must be a valid, writable cc_string buffer capable of holding the formatted text
action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL) describing the operation that failed
path must point to a valid, initialized cc_string representing the path to include in the message (non-NULL)
describeErr, if non-NULL, must be a function matching Logger_DescribeError and safe to call with (res, dst)
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_Warn
functions.signature: void Logger_Warn(cc_result res, const char* action, Logger_DescribeError describeErr);
functions.description: Informs the user about a non-fatal error. May show a dialog or route to in-game chat depending on runtime state. Optionally appends a human-readable description from describeErr.
requirements: action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL) describing the failed action
describeErr, if non-NULL, must be a function matching Logger_DescribeError and safe to call with (res, dst)
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_Warn2
functions.signature: void Logger_Warn2(cc_result res, const char* action, const cc_string* path, Logger_DescribeError describeErr);
functions.description: Informs the user about a non-fatal error involving a specific path. May show a dialog or route to in-game chat. Optionally appends a human-readable description from describeErr.
requirements: action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL) describing the failed action
path must point to a valid, initialized cc_string representing the path (non-NULL)
describeErr, if non-NULL, must be a function matching Logger_DescribeError and safe to call with (res, dst)
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_SimpleWarn
functions.signature: void Logger_SimpleWarn(cc_result res, const char* action);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for Logger_Warn without an error describer. Notifies the user of a non-fatal error in action.
requirements: action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL)
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_SimpleWarn2
functions.signature: void Logger_SimpleWarn2(cc_result res, const char* action, const cc_string* path);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for Logger_Warn2 without an error describer. Notifies the user of a non-fatal error for a specific path.
requirements: action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL)
path must point to a valid, initialized cc_string (non-NULL)
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_DynamicLibWarn
functions.signature: void Logger_DynamicLibWarn(const char* action, const cc_string* path);
functions.description: Shows a warning for a failed DynamicLib_Load2/Get2 call. Formats as: "Error [action] '[path]'\n  Error meaning: [desc]" with an appropriate system-provided description.
requirements: action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL) indicating the dynamic library action
path must point to a valid, initialized cc_string representing the library path or symbol (non-NULL)

functions.name: Logger_SysWarn
functions.signature: void Logger_SysWarn(cc_result res, const char* action);
functions.description: Shortcut for Logger_Warn using Platform_DescribeError to provide a system error description.
requirements: action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL)
relies on the presence of Platform_DescribeError in the platform layer
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_SysWarn2
functions.signature: void Logger_SysWarn2(cc_result res, const char* action, const cc_string* path);
functions.description: Shortcut for Logger_Warn2 using Platform_DescribeError to provide a system error description.
requirements: action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL)
path must point to a valid, initialized cc_string (non-NULL)
relies on the presence of Platform_DescribeError in the platform layer
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_IOWarn2
functions.signature: void Logger_IOWarn2(cc_result res, const char* action, const struct cc_filepath_* path);
functions.description: Shortcut for Logger_Warn2 tailored for I/O operations, using Platform_DescribeError and a cc_filepath_ path.
requirements: action must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL)
path must point to a valid cc_filepath_ object (non-NULL) as required by I/O routines
relies on the presence of Platform_DescribeError in the platform layer
res is an error/result code; no specific range constraints stated

functions.name: Logger_Backtrace
functions.signature: void Logger_Backtrace(cc_string* trace, void* ctx);
functions.description: Generates a backtrace string based on the platform-specific CPU context ctx and writes it to trace. Note: the provided CPU context may be modified on some platforms (e.g., Windows).
requirements: trace must be a valid, writable cc_string buffer capable of receiving the backtrace text
ctx must be a platform-specific CPU context pointer appropriate for the current platform; it may be modified during the call

functions.name: Logger_Log
functions.signature: void Logger_Log(const cc_string* msg);
functions.description: Appends msg to client.log on disk. The message is written raw and is not converted to Unicode (unlike Stream_WriteLine).
requirements: msg must point to a valid, initialized cc_string containing the text to log (non-NULL)
callers should ensure msg’s encoding is suitable for raw output (no Unicode conversion performed)

functions.name: Logger_Hook
functions.signature: void Logger_Hook(void);
functions.description: Initializes or installs logger-related hooks. Typical usage is during startup to set platform-specific logging behavior. Exact behavior is not documented in this header.
requirements: may need to be called during application initialization/startup; exact timing requirements are not documented
no parameters; side effects depend on platform-specific implementation

functions.name: Logger_DoAbort
functions.signature: void Logger_DoAbort(cc_result result, const char* raw_msg, void* ctx);
functions.description: Performs a fatal-error abort with the given result code, raw C-string message, and optional CPU context for backtrace/logging. Intended to terminate execution after logging/reporting the error.
requirements: raw_msg must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL) containing an unformatted message
ctx is a platform-specific CPU context pointer; usage/format is platform-dependent and may be optional
function likely does not return (abort semantics), but this is not explicitly stated in the header

functions.name: Logger_FailToStart
functions.signature: void Logger_FailToStart(const char* raw_msg);
functions.description: Reports a fatal error that prevented the program from starting, using the provided raw C-string message. Typically shows a fatal dialog and exits; exact behavior is not documented in this header.
requirements: raw_msg must be a valid, null-terminated C string (non-NULL)

functions.name: String_CalcLen
functions.signature: CC_API int String_CalcLen(const char* raw, int capacity);
functions.description: Counts characters in a non-owning C string until a '\0' or until capacity is reached. Useful for determining length of a possibly unterminated buffer segment.
requirements: raw must be a valid pointer to at least capacity bytes of readable memory
capacity must be >= 0
Stops early if a '\0' byte is encountered

functions.name: String_Length
functions.signature: int String_Length(const char* raw);
functions.description: Counts characters in a null-terminated C string until the terminating '\0'.
requirements: raw must point to a valid null-terminated string
Memory must be readable up to and including the first '\0'

functions.name: String_FromRaw
functions.signature: CC_NOINLINE cc_string String_FromRaw(STRING_REF char* buffer, int capacity);
functions.description: Constructs a cc_string that references a writable buffer of known capacity whose actual string content may or may not be null-terminated.
requirements: buffer must be a valid writable pointer to at least capacity bytes
capacity must be >= 0
Resulting cc_string does not own the memory; caller must keep buffer alive for the lifetime of the cc_string
Initial length is computed from buffer content up to capacity (may stop at '\0')

functions.name: String_FromReadonly
functions.signature: CC_API cc_string String_FromReadonly(STRING_REF const char* buffer);
functions.description: Constructs a cc_string that references a null-terminated constant read-only buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated string
The resulting cc_string must not be modified through APIs that write to its buffer
Caller must keep buffer alive for the lifetime of the cc_string

functions.name: String_Copy
functions.signature: CC_API void String_Copy(cc_string* dst, const cc_string* src);
functions.description: Resets dst length to 0, then appends all characters from src into dst.
requirements: dst must reference a writable buffer with sufficient capacity to hold src->length characters
dst and src must be non-null valid cc_string pointers
If dst->capacity < src->length, excess characters will be truncated by append behavior (implementation-defined); ensure sufficient capacity to avoid data loss

functions.name: String_CopyToRaw
functions.signature: int String_CopyToRaw(char* dst, int capacity, const cc_string* src);
functions.description: Copies up to capacity characters from src into dst. Appends a '\0' only if src->length < capacity. Intended for fixed-size arrays via String_CopyToRawArray.
requirements: dst must be a valid writable pointer to at least capacity bytes
capacity must be >= 0
src must be a valid cc_string pointer
Caller must not assume dst is null-terminated unless src->length < capacity
Recommended to use only with buffers created via String_FromRawArray as noted

functions.name: String_UNSAFE_Substring
functions.signature: CC_API cc_string String_UNSAFE_Substring(STRING_REF const cc_string* str, int offset, int length);
functions.description: Returns a substring view whose buffer points inside str.buffer. Does not allocate or copy. Marked UNSAFE because the returned cc_string shares memory with the source.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
offset and length must designate a range fully within [0, str->length]
Caller must keep the original string's backing buffer alive and unmodified in the relevant region while using the substring
Returned cc_string must not outlive or be used after the base buffer is invalidated or reallocated

functions.name: String_UNSAFE_SubstringAt
functions.signature: CC_API cc_string String_UNSAFE_SubstringAt(STRING_REF const cc_string* str, int offset);
functions.description: Returns a substring view from offset to end. The sub.buffer is str.buffer + offset and sub.length is str.length - offset. Shares memory with str.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
offset must satisfy 0 <= offset <= str->length
Caller must keep the original buffer alive; returned substring is non-owning and aliasing
Do not modify or free memory underlying str while the substring is in use

functions.name: String_UNSAFE_Split
functions.signature: CC_API int String_UNSAFE_Split(STRING_REF const cc_string* str, char c, cc_string* subs, int maxSubs);
functions.description: Splits str by delimiter c into up to maxSubs substring views stored in subs. Returns the number of substrings found. Substrings alias the original buffer.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
subs must point to an array of at least maxSubs cc_string elements
maxSubs must be >= 0
Returned substrings reference str.buffer; keep the original buffer alive and unchanged while using them

functions.name: String_UNSAFE_SplitBy
functions.signature: CC_API void String_UNSAFE_SplitBy(STRING_REF cc_string* str, char c, cc_string* part);
functions.description: Splits str into [part][c][rest]. Writes the segment before c into part and mutates str to become the remainder after c. Intended for repeated calls until str->length is 0.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string and will be modified in-place (buffer/length adjustments)
part must be a valid cc_string pointer to receive a substring view
Returned views alias the original buffer; keep the buffer alive and unchanged except for sanctioned pointer/length adjustments

functions.name: String_UNSAFE_Separate
functions.signature: CC_API int String_UNSAFE_Separate(STRING_REF const cc_string* str, char c, cc_string* key, cc_string* value);
functions.description: Splits str into key and value around the first delimiter c, trimming a space before value as in examples (e.g., "allowed =true" -> key="allowed", value="true"). Returns non-zero if c was found; otherwise sets key=str and value=String_Empty and returns 0. Returned substrings alias the original buffer.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
key and value must be non-null pointers to cc_string to receive substring views
Caller must keep the original buffer alive while using key/value substrings

functions.name: String_Equals
functions.signature: CC_API int String_Equals(const cc_string* a, const cc_string* b);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if two cc_strings are exactly equal in length and characters (case-sensitive).
requirements: a and b must be valid cc_string pointers

functions.name: String_CaselessEquals
functions.signature: CC_API int String_CaselessEquals(const cc_string* a, const cc_string* b);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if two strings are equal ignoring ASCII case.
requirements: a and b must be valid cc_string pointers

functions.name: String_CaselessEqualsConst
functions.signature: CC_API int String_CaselessEqualsConst(const cc_string* a, const char* b);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if cc_string a equals C-string b ignoring ASCII case. Optimised compared to constructing a cc_string for b.
requirements: a must be a valid cc_string pointer
b must be a valid null-terminated C string

functions.name: String_MakeUInt32
functions.signature: int String_MakeUInt32(cc_uint32 num, char* digits);
functions.description: Breaks a 32-bit unsigned integer into its decimal digits stored in reverse order into digits. Returns the number of digits written.
requirements: digits must point to a buffer large enough to hold up to 10 digits for a 32-bit value
digits are written in reverse order (least significant first) as documented

functions.name: String_Append
functions.signature: CC_API void String_Append(cc_string* str, char c);
functions.description: Attempts to append a single character to str. No-op if str->length == str->capacity.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string referencing a writable buffer
str->capacity must correctly reflect writable space; append is ignored if full

functions.name: String_AppendBool
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendBool(cc_string* str, cc_bool value);
functions.description: Appends "true" if value is non-zero, otherwise "false", truncated if necessary by available capacity.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer

functions.name: String_AppendInt
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendInt(cc_string* str, int num);
functions.description: Appends the decimal representation of a signed integer (with leading '-' for negatives).
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
May truncate if insufficient capacity; ensure space for all digits and optional sign to avoid truncation

functions.name: String_AppendUInt32
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendUInt32(cc_string* str, cc_uint32 num);
functions.description: Appends the decimal representation of an unsigned 32-bit integer.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
Ensure sufficient capacity to avoid truncation

functions.name: String_AppendPaddedInt
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendPaddedInt(cc_string* str, int num, int minDigits);
functions.description: Appends a signed integer with left-zero padding to at least minDigits digits.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
minDigits should be >= 0

functions.name: String_AppendFloat
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendFloat(cc_string* str, float num, int fracDigits);
functions.description: Appends a floating-point number. If num is an integer, no decimal point is added; otherwise exactly fracDigits digits are added after a decimal point. Example: 2.6745f with fracDigits=2 yields "2.67".
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
fracDigits should be >= 0
Locale-specific decimal separators are not handled (todo in code comment); assumes '.'

functions.name: String_AppendConst
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendConst(cc_string* str, const char* src);
functions.description: Appends characters from a null-terminated C string to str.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
src must be a valid null-terminated C string

functions.name: String_AppendAll
functions.signature: void String_AppendAll(cc_string* str, const void* data, int len);
functions.description: Appends len raw bytes from data to str.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory
len must be >= 0

functions.name: String_AppendString
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendString(cc_string* str, const cc_string* src);
functions.description: Appends all characters from src to str.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
src must be a valid cc_string

functions.name: String_AppendColorless
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendColorless(cc_string* str, const cc_string* src);
functions.description: Appends characters from src to str while skipping any embedded color codes. Exact color code format is project-specific.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
src must be a valid cc_string
Color code rules are implementation-defined; caller should not rely on specific stripping behavior beyond skipping color codes

functions.name: String_AppendHex
functions.signature: CC_API void String_AppendHex(cc_string* str, cc_uint8 value);
functions.description: Appends the two hexadecimal digits representing the byte value (00-FF).
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer

functions.name: String_IndexOfAt
functions.signature: CC_API int String_IndexOfAt(const cc_string* str, int offset, char c);
functions.description: Finds the first index of character c in str at or after offset. Returns -1 if not found.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
offset must be in range [0, str->length]

functions.name: String_LastIndexOfAt
functions.signature: CC_API int String_LastIndexOfAt(const cc_string* str, int offset, char c);
functions.description: Finds the last index of character c in str, starting search at or after offset according to implementation. Returns -1 if not found.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
offset should be in range [0, str->length]

functions.name: String_InsertAt
functions.signature: CC_API void String_InsertAt(cc_string* str, int offset, char c);
functions.description: Inserts character c at position offset within str, shifting subsequent characters. Exits the process if insertion fails.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
offset must be in range [0, str->length]
str must have capacity for one more character; failure causes process termination

functions.name: String_DeleteAt
functions.signature: CC_API void String_DeleteAt(cc_string* str, int offset);
functions.description: Deletes the character at position offset, shifting subsequent characters left. Exits the process if deletion fails.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
offset must be in range [0, str->length - 1]

functions.name: String_UNSAFE_TrimStart
functions.signature: CC_API void String_UNSAFE_TrimStart(cc_string* str);
functions.description: Trims leading spaces by adjusting buffer pointer and length; underlying memory is not shifted. Marked UNSAFE due to aliasing/lifetime implications.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
Subsequent operations must account that str.buffer may be advanced into the original buffer
Do not rely on original leading characters remaining addressable via str

functions.name: String_UNSAFE_TrimEnd
functions.signature: CC_API void String_UNSAFE_TrimEnd(cc_string* str);
functions.description: Trims trailing spaces by reducing length; underlying memory is not shifted. Marked UNSAFE because it mutates view without moving memory.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
Only trailing spaces are removed; buffer content remains but length is reduced

functions.name: String_IndexOfConst
functions.signature: CC_API int String_IndexOfConst(const cc_string* str, const char* sub);
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of null-terminated substring sub in str. Returns -1 if not found.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string
sub must be a valid null-terminated C string

functions.name: String_CaselessContains
functions.signature: CC_API int String_CaselessContains(const cc_string* str, const cc_string* sub);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if sub occurs within str ignoring ASCII case.
requirements: str and sub must be valid cc_string pointers

functions.name: String_CaselessStarts
functions.signature: CC_API int String_CaselessStarts(const cc_string* str, const cc_string* sub);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if str starts with sub ignoring ASCII case.
requirements: str and sub must be valid cc_string pointers

functions.name: String_CaselessEnds
functions.signature: CC_API int String_CaselessEnds(const cc_string* str, const cc_string* sub);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if str ends with sub ignoring ASCII case.
requirements: str and sub must be valid cc_string pointers

functions.name: String_Compare
functions.signature: CC_API int String_Compare(const cc_string* a, const cc_string* b);
functions.description: Compares two strings first by length, then lexicographically if lengths equal. Returns negative if a<b, positive if a>b, 0 if equal. Magnitude is not restricted to -1/0/1.
requirements: a and b must be valid cc_string pointers

functions.name: String_Format1
functions.signature: CC_API void String_Format1(cc_string* str, const char* format, const void* a1);
functions.description: Formats into str according to the custom format string using one argument. Low-level API: no runtime type/count checking beyond this function variant. Supports specifiers: %b, %i, %f[0-9], %p[0-9], %t, %c, %s, %r, %x, %h.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
format must be a valid null-terminated C string
a1 must point to a value of the exact type required by the first specifier in format
Caller is responsible for matching specifiers to argument types; mismatch is undefined

functions.name: String_Format2
functions.signature: CC_API void String_Format2(cc_string* str, const char* format, const void* a1, const void* a2);
functions.description: Formats into str using two untyped arguments according to the format string. Same specifiers as String_Format1.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
format must be a valid null-terminated C string
a1 and a2 must point to values matching the first and second specifiers respectively
Caller must ensure argument types and count match the format string

functions.name: String_Format3
functions.signature: CC_API void String_Format3(cc_string* str, const char* format, const void* a1, const void* a2, const void* a3);
functions.description: Formats into str using three untyped arguments. Same behavior and specifiers as String_Format1.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
format must be a valid null-terminated C string
a1, a2, a3 must match the first three specifiers in format

functions.name: String_Format4
functions.signature: CC_API void String_Format4(cc_string* str, const char* format, const void* a1, const void* a2, const void* a3, const void* a4);
functions.description: Formats into str using up to four untyped arguments. Low-level API similar to printf/String.Format with listed specifiers. No type/count checking performed.
requirements: str must be a valid cc_string with writable buffer
format must be a valid null-terminated C string
a1..a4 must point to values whose types match the corresponding specifiers in format
Caller must ensure enough capacity in str to hold the formatted result or accept truncation as per append semantics

functions.name: Convert_CP437ToUnicode
functions.signature: cc_unichar Convert_CP437ToUnicode(char c);
functions.description: Maps a single CP437-encoded character to its Unicode code unit equivalent.
requirements: Input c is interpreted as a CP437 character (0-255 effectively via char)

functions.name: Convert_CodepointToCP437
functions.signature: char Convert_CodepointToCP437(cc_codepoint cp);
functions.description: Maps a Unicode code point to the closest CP437 character. Returns '?' if there is no mapping.
requirements: cp must be a valid Unicode code point

functions.name: Convert_TryCodepointToCP437
functions.signature: CC_API cc_bool Convert_TryCodepointToCP437(cc_codepoint cp, char* c);
functions.description: Attempts to map a Unicode code point to a CP437 character. Returns non-zero on success and writes the mapped character to *c.
requirements: c must be a valid non-null pointer for output
cp must be a valid Unicode code point

functions.name: Convert_Utf8ToCodepoint
functions.signature: int Convert_Utf8ToCodepoint(cc_codepoint* cp, const cc_uint8* data, cc_uint32 len);
functions.description: Decodes one Unicode code point from a UTF-8 byte sequence. Returns number of bytes consumed, or 0 if not enough input is available to read a full character.
requirements: cp must be a valid non-null pointer to receive the decoded code point
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory
len is the number of available bytes; function returns 0 if incomplete sequence

functions.name: Convert_CP437ToUtf8
functions.signature: int Convert_CP437ToUtf8(char c, cc_uint8* data);
functions.description: Encodes a CP437 character as UTF-8 into data. Returns the number of bytes written (1, 2, or 3).
requirements: data must point to a buffer with space for at least 3 bytes
